summary: Opaque native addon with browser-credential and cookie stealer fingerprints
details: Package ships a single stripped 10.4 MB Rust-compiled Node-API binary (`tools.linux-x64-gnu.node`) as `main`, so `require()` of the package hands control to the addon on the installer's host. Extracted strings from the binary include browser-credential and cookie database indicators (`Found login for`, `on Cookie.value when inserting`, `TSQLITE_AUTH_USER`), an embedded TLS HTTP client stack (`ureq_proto::util`, sqlite, zstd), and host-enumeration primitives (`getifaddrs`, `gethostname`, `/etc/lsb-release`, `/dev/disk/by-id/`, CPU/bogomips readers). The name and version string (`new-native-tools-linux-x64-gnu@3.1.40-chrom-381-new-browser-icons-367-...`) mimic the per-platform prebuild naming scheme used by legitimate native-addon families (e.g. `@napi-rs/*-linux-x64-gnu`), but the package has no publisher identity, no repository, no homepage, no scripts, and a one-sentence README that does not describe what the binary does. The combination of a generically-named opaque native payload, browser Login Data / Cookies SQLite access strings, host fingerprinting, and an outbound HTTPS client is the shape of a browser-credential stealer delivered as a masquerading prebuild.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
